title.narrative: Emergency response to vulnerable people affected by the earthquake in Vanuatu

description.narrative: According to the latest results of the assessment conducted by the Displacement and Evacuation Centre Management (DECM) Cluster co-led by the National Disaster Management Office (NDMO) and IOM, 2,435 people are displaced (838 people are living in six evacuation centers and 1,597 people are living in 67 host households) as of 24 December 2024. The assessment highlights a large spectrum of unmet needs presented by the affected population including water, food, medical supplies, lighting, tarpaulins and shelter kits. The assessment also identified that fear of returning remains high due to damaged housing and road conditions, as well as post-disaster trauma, self-identified by the population as relating to fear of another earthquake or tsunami, with many expecting to remain displaced for at least a month. With the support from CERF, IOM in collaboration with the NDMO will support 119 vulnerable households inclusive of 595 individuals that were affected by the earthquake, with cash for shelter modality, monitoring of displaced populations and technical assistance to the DECM Cluster, evacuation centers and affected households including engineering assessment of building structure of evacuation centers and houses. IOM will undertake the following key interventions:Provide cash for shelter assistance to target 119 vulnerable households to meet the immediate needs of the affected populations whose homes were destroyed or damaged by the earthquake.Gather and analyse multi-sectoral data on the mobility, vulnerabilities, and needs of earthquake-affected populations that enables decision makers and responders, including all clusters, to provide these populations with better life saving assistance.Technical support to the Vanuatu DECM Cluster and Shelter Cluster in their objective to support the voluntary return of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in a safe and dignified manner. It includes engineering support / assessments of building structures including evacuation centres and houses to ensure build back safer techniques are utilised by the affected population.Through this project, IOM, in coordination with the NDMO, clusters, Cash Working Group (CWG), the Shefa Provincial Government and Area Councils, and Vanuatu Red Cross Society aims to deliver life-saving assistance to people affected by the earthquake. Selection of beneficiaries will be based on vulnerability criterion agreed with NDMO, DECM Cluster, Shelter Cluster and partners. The project will prioritize the specific vulnerable groups including people with disabilities, older persons, pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers and other groups of individuals with specific needs among the affected population.Through its support of ongoing displacement tracking of evacuation centres and host households, which includes collection of data across a range of cross-sectoral indicators across WASH, Shelter, Gender and Protection and Food Security Clusters, IOM will coordinate with UNFPA and UNICEF to ensure that displacement sites reporting relevant vulnerabilities and needs related to WASH, PSS, protection-related vulnerabilities are referred and addressed with the assistance of CERF funding.
